paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation:
The plot illustrates the relationship between turn number and average change percentage, separated by initial answer type. The x-axis is labeled "Turn Number" and has a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled "Average Change Percentage (%)" and has a linear scale ranging from 0 to 50, with tick labels at 10-unit intervals. 

The first line, representing "Initial Correct Answer," is red with circular markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 17% at turn number 1, increases to roughly 24% at turn number 4, then remains steady at approximately 12% from turn number 4 through turn number 7. The second line, representing "Initial Incorrect Answer," is orange with circular markers and a solid line style. It begins at approximately 15% at turn number 1, rises sharply to approximately 41% at turn number 2, continues to roughly 26% at turn number 3, then plateaus at approximately 26% from turn number 3 through turn number 7.
